key_insight: FMRP-LEAN turns a manually tracked clinical assay workflow into a state-explicit, HIPAA-compliant LIMS with AI support, improving visibility and coordination across the full biospecimen lifecycle.
engineering_relevance: The architecture shows how regulated translational labs can combine finite-state workflow control, secure data residency, and interoperable systems to reduce operational risk in multi-day assays.
method: Finite-state workflow model with explicit transition guards and dwell-time tracking
Self-hosted Supabase/PostgreSQL stack inside hospital-controlled infrastructure with encrypted tunneling and loopback-only services
Bi-directional REDCap sync plus MRN-UUIDv7 and QR-based specimen tracking
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved workflow observability, reduced QC latency, and greater cross-role transparency after deployment.
watch_item: The AI module is constrained to aggregate projections and deterministic fallbacks, so real-world benefit may depend on careful validation of governance, interoperability, and staff adoption.
paper_title: FMRP-LEAN: A HIPAA-Compliant AI-Augmented LIMS Architecture for End-to-End Clinical Assay Workflow Optimization
